data.title: Mometasone furoate 0.1% (cream, ointment, lotion)
data.summary: IV Topical corticosteroids · Medium (cream, US class 4) to high (ointment, class 2) potency non-fluorinated (chlorinated) steroid; 'soft steroid'
data.body:
_Topicals · IV Topical corticosteroids_

**Class:** Medium (cream, US class 4) to high (ointment, class 2) potency non-fluorinated (chlorinated) steroid; 'soft steroid'

## Mechanism of action
- Potent glucocorticoid receptor agonist with high skin activity but low systemic bioavailability (rapid hepatic breakdown)
- Favourable ratio of benefit to atrophy

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Atopic dermatitis, psoriasis (including scalp — lotion), lichen planus, discoid lupus, seborrhoeic dermatitis
- Children over 2 years (short courses), and limited face use under supervision
- Proactive twice-weekly maintenance in atopic dermatitis

## Dose & formulations
- Once daily (its long skin activity allows single daily application)
- Children: avoid long courses, large areas and occlusion

## Adverse effects
- Atrophy, striae, perioral dermatitis with misuse (lower than other potent steroids)
- Widely misused in India in fairness/combination creams

## Contraindications
- As for topical steroids; avoid in nappy area under occlusion

## Pregnancy & lactation
Use on limited areas for short periods.

## Viva points
- Once-daily 'soft' steroid with low systemic absorption
- Cream class 4 vs ointment class 2 — vehicle changes potency

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.45; Khopkar ch.22. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
